judge_assessment.explanation: Both hard failures reproduce exactly against the artifacts. Problem 3 prints three requested responses - g(-2), which piece of p that selects and why, and p(g(-2)) - and verify.json id 3 is a single eval ((2*x+1)**2 at x=-2, expected 9) covering only the third. Problem 7(b) asks for (p o g)(x) as a two-branch piecewise rule with the correct inequalities; id 7 verifies only the cut point x = 1/2. Problem 8(b), problem 10(b)'s domain [4, inf), and problem 11(b)'s interval-notation domain are all printed responses with no verify entry. Problem 12 is the sharpest instance: the worksheet asks for "the complete solution set" and the two id-12 entries are the raw per-piece root sets. The judge's second claim is also exact - problems 5, 6 and 9 each end with an explicit "say in one line" or "state ... what that says about whether composition is commutative" request, verify.json contains zero entries of type manual, machine_observation.gate_chain_manual_flags is false, and final_response.md states "Nothing is flagged for manual review." Beyond the judge: the answer key's Quick Answers bank prints "12. -3, -3/2, 1/2", banking x = -3/2 - the candidate the whole problem exists to teach students to reject - as an answer, in direct contradiction of the key body three inches below it ("Complete solution set: x = -3 and x = 1/2"). The judge scored mathematical_correctness 4/4 and reported that all solutions agree with the key; that specific claim is wrong for the banked form of problem 12.

strengths_to_preserve: The single shared function library (f, g, h and the piecewise p, q defined once above problem 1) lets every later problem reuse an earlier result - a wrong rule in problem 2 resurfaces in problem 4 - which is how a real unit compounds rather than a list of disconnected items.

Problem 7 is a genuinely well-chosen item: p breaks at input 2, but under the inner map g(x) = 2x+1 the break of (p o g) moves to x = 1/2. That one design decision teaches exactly what students get wrong about piecewise composition, and the key's closing line ("the inner function moves it") names it.

Problems 1 and 5 are the same two functions in opposite order (22 versus 13) and problems 2 and 6 are their rules (4x^2+4x-2 versus 2x^2-5). Non-commutativity is demonstrated with four cheap computations instead of asserted.

The four declared traps all evaluate to values distinguishable from the right answer (3 vs 22, 8 vs 9, 46 vs 13, 5 vs 2) and print in the key's Common wrong answers block against the right problem numbers.

Problem 10 pairs the simplification f(h(x)) = x - 7 with the domain [4, inf) it discards, and the key adds "a line with its left half deleted, not a line" - the best one-sentence statement of that idea anywhere in this shard.

root_causes.description: SKILL.md line 189 states the contract as "verification hard-fails unless every problem id 1..N has at least one check". The unit of coverage is the problem id, not the printed answer slot, so a problem that prints three responses satisfies the gate with one. Every uncovered slot in this case sits under an id that already has a passing check.
evidence: SKILL.md:189 - 'every problem id 1..N has at least one check'
worksheet problem 3 prints three requested responses; verify.json id 3 holds one eval entry
worksheet problem 7(b) asks for a two-branch piecewise rule; verify.json id 7 holds only solve 2*x+1-2 -> 1/2
gate_log.txt records verify-ws PASS and the run ends 'BUILD PASSED - all gates green'

root_causes.description: SKILL.md line 249 tells the author to reframe understanding topics through the ordinary checkable types and to "Reserve manual for genuinely open reasoning". Read as written, a problem that ends in a computed value looks fully handled even when it also demands a sentence. The author followed the instruction and produced a 12-problem sheet with nine explanation requests and zero manual entries.

verify.json contains no entry with type manual despite task_contract.verification_targets including 'manual' and review_mode 'manual_allowed'

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers.render_entry concatenates every verify entry sharing a problem id with no notion of which values survive the problem's own validity test. Problem 12's two entries are the per-piece root sets, so the bank prints the rejected candidate -3/2 beside the two real solutions.

improvements.title: Bind verification to every printed answer slot, not to one check per problem id
improvements.proposed_change: Change the coverage unit from problem id to printed answer slot. Have the worksheet-side gate count answer locations per problem (the \problem auto-blank plus every \ansline / \answerline / \ansblank inside that block, plus each enumerated sub-part that ends in a request) and require the verify entries for that id to cover at least that many responses, counting manual entries. Restate SKILL.md line 189 in those terms: one check per response the student writes, not one per problem.
improvements.regression_test: Add a tests/fixtures case with a two-slot problem: the worksheet prints "(a) find the value ... (b) write the rule" under one \problem id while verify.json carries a single entry for that id. A new answer-slot gate must exit non-zero naming the id and the uncovered slot. Today build.sh exits 0 on exactly this shape, so the test fails before the fix and passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: Directly addresses problems 3, 7, 8, 10, 11 and 12 here and the same shape in curr-406, curr-419, curr-426, curr-438, curr-444 and curr-450. This is the single largest source of REJECTs in the shard.
improvements.risk: Slot counting from prose is heuristic; an over-eager counter could fail well-formed sheets. Mitigate by counting enumerated sub-parts and explicit "write ... on the answer line" phrases only, and by shipping the first release at exit 2 (manual review) rather than exit 1.

improvements.title: Require a manual entry whenever a problem asks the student to explain, name or justify
improvements.proposed_change: Amend SKILL.md line 249 so the reframing advice is explicitly about the corrected VALUE, and add the missing half: when a problem also asks the student to name the error, state which piece applies and why, or say what a comparison shows, that request is a second response and must carry its own manual entry with the model answer in desc. Add a build gate that fails a verify.json whose problem stem contains an explain-class imperative but has no manual entry for that id.
improvements.regression_test: Add tests/check_manual_coverage.py plus a fixture whose problem stem contains an explain-class imperative (explain / justify / name the error / say in words / state whether) while its verify.json id has no entry of type manual. The gate must exit non-zero. I ran this exact lint over the ten cases in this shard: it fires on curr-402 (7 ids), curr-406 (4), curr-419 (5), curr-426 (2), curr-438 (5) and curr-450 (3), and stays silent on all three ACCEPTs (curr-413, curr-425, curr-432) - zero false positives. Fails before the fix, passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: Problems 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12 would each gain a manual entry, the build would exit 2 instead of 0, and final_response.md could no longer claim 'Nothing is flagged for manual review' on a sheet with nine written justifications.
improvements.risk: Verb-list linting will miss paraphrases ("what does that tell you about ...") and could nag on stems that merely narrate. Keep the list short, allow an explicit per-problem opt-out field in the JSON, and ship at exit 2 first.

improvements.title: Verify the piece-selection condition and the surviving candidate set, not the raw per-piece roots
improvements.proposed_change: For piecewise and candidate-validity problems, let a verify entry carry the condition that selects the branch (for example a 'where' field such as '2*x+1 < 0') so verify.py can discard roots that fall outside the region where that piece is in force, and add a final entry holding the complete solution set the answer line actually asks for. Problem 12's second entry would then yield ['1/2'] rather than ['-3/2', '1/2'], and a third entry would verify {-3, 1/2}.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture: a piecewise equation q(g(x)) = 5 whose second branch has an extraneous root outside its own region. verify.py must reject an expected list that includes the extraneous root once a condition field is declared, and must accept the filtered set. Fails today because verify.py has no notion of a branch condition.
improvements.expected_impact: Problems 3, 7, 8 and 12 move inside the verification boundary, and the answer key can no longer bank a value the key body rejects.
improvements.risk: Adding a condition field widens verify.py's schema surface; the strict allowlist must be extended carefully so a malformed condition is a hard failure rather than a silent skip.

improvements.title: Verify the domain a simplification discards, not only the reduced expression
improvements.proposed_change: When an equiv entry records a simplification that loses a restriction, require a companion entry (or a 'domain' field on the equiv) holding the restriction the student must state. Problem 10 verifies (sqrt(x-4))**2-3 == x-7 and leaves [4, inf) unchecked; problem 11 verifies the boundary roots +/-sqrt(7) and leaves the two-piece interval-notation domain unchecked. Both are printed answers.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture: equiv on (sqrt(x-4))**2-3 with expected 'x-7' and no declared domain, where the worksheet stem asks for the domain. The gate must fail until a domain entry is present. Passes today.
improvements.expected_impact: Closes the exact gap the judge called 'a simplification loses an excluded value'; applies to every composition, rational-function and radical sheet in the suite.
improvements.risk: Domain notation is not uniquely canonical ([4, inf) versus x >= 4), so the checker must compare sets via sympy rather than strings or it will produce false failures.

improvements.title: Stop the Quick Answers bank printing a candidate the answer key explicitly rejects
improvements.proposed_change: render_entry currently joins every expected value under a problem id. Give verify entries an optional 'bank': false (or an 'extraneous' marker on individual expected values) so intermediate per-branch root sets stay out of the grading bank, and have render_quick_answers cross-check the banked line against the answer key's boxed final answer for that problem, warning when the bank carries a value the key does not box.
improvements.regression_test: Extend tests/test_render_quick_answers.py with two entries under one id, the second holding an expected value marked extraneous. Assert the rendered bank line is '-3, 1/2' and not '-3, -3/2, 1/2'. Fails today: render_entry joins unconditionally.
improvements.expected_impact: A student self-checking against the bank currently reads x = -3/2 as correct, which is precisely the misconception problem 12 was built to eliminate. The fix removes an artifact that actively teaches the error.
improvements.risk: A 'bank: false' flag could be used to hide answers that should be shown; pair it with a warning when more than a third of a sheet's entries opt out.

case_summary: A strong composition sheet undone by its verification boundary. The mathematics is right everywhere I checked it - (f o g)(2) = 22, (g o f)(3) = 13, 4x^2+4x-2 versus 2x^2-5, x = -5/2 and 3/2, x = +/-5, x - 7 on [4, inf), +/-sqrt(7), and the {-3, 1/2} solution set - and the key's reasoning is genuinely instructive. But the sheet prints roughly twenty responses across twelve problems and verifies thirteen of them, with nine written justifications recorded as verified rather than manual. Two defects sit under that: the coverage contract is per problem id, and SKILL.md's reframing advice implies a computed value settles an item that also demands a sentence. One defect the judge did not catch is worse than the coverage gaps: the Quick Answers bank prints x = -3/2 for problem 12, the candidate the answer key rejects two paragraphs earlier, so the at-a-glance grading column teaches the exact error the problem was designed to expose.
